limits: Public-kernel end-to-end fixtures use VLESS on one physical node; other protocols, non-root socket access and other kernels are not declared verified. Secret/retired-hash attribution has focused tests.
Exhaustion verifies real metering settlement/new connection denial and positive control; it does not measure cross-node overuse or a held connection in that specific scenario.
Native command timeout/ACK loss remains pending; no atomic transaction spans the database and kernel. Fresh native observation and scoped retry recover uncertain effects.
Subscription/credential fence may hold a DB write/row lock for at most a 3-second command context. Cost under load has not been benchmarked.
End-to-end timings include scheduled polling and concurrent isolated workloads; these are individual observations, not latency or throughput guarantees.
Active principal/credential compatibility lookup, native frame, per-principal batch, total command and time budgets deliberately defer beyond coverage; unknown ownership does not close a connection.
Restore/swap entitlement epochs, per-credential delivery proof, full refund/autorenew/discount rules and P4-P7 remain incomplete.
No production database migration, real external payment/refund, release, deployment, merge or other repository modification performed.

The subscription/credential fence does not establish atomicity with independent node-group regrant edits. Those interleavings, deleted-resource ownership retention, and indexed attribution beyond 4096 retained credentials remain P3 work; no complete P3 claim is made.
